source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: From Bretton Woods to the Nixon shock to the petrodollar arrangement. The US dollar's journey to global reserve status. The dollar system provides real stability and liquidity that the world depends on. But it creates asymmetric vulnerability for peripheral economies: oil priced in dollars, debt denominated in dollars, vulnerability to Federal Reserve decisions made with American interests in mind. This episode traces how reserve currency status works in practice, what "exorbitant privilege" actually means, and how Muslim-majority economies navigate a system they didn't design but can't avoid.

thread: Reserve currency status is empire by other means. The world prices oil in dollars, borrows in dollars, then watches the Federal Reserve make decisions for American workers in Michigan.
Bretton Woods promised gold convertibility. Nixon ended that in 1971. What remained was a system where everyone needed dollars but only America could print them.
The petrodollar arrangement sealed it. Oil producers would price crude in dollars, park the proceeds in US Treasury bonds. The world's most essential commodity became America's monetary anchor.

linkedin.post: The dollar's global reserve status creates a peculiar form of economic sovereignty. While it provides real stability and liquidity that the world depends on, it also means that Federal Reserve decisions made with American workers in mind ripple through every economy that trades in dollars—which is almost all of them. From Bretton Woods to the Nixon shock to the petrodollar arrangement, the dollar's journey to reserve currency status wasn't inevitable. But once established, it created what economists call "exorbitant privilege"—the ability to borrow in your own currency while others must navigate exchange rate risk. For Muslim-majority economies, this system presents daily asymmetries: oil priced in dollars, debt denominated in dollars, vulnerability to monetary policy designed for different economic priorities. Listen: https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-mm-3

instagram.caption: The dollar became the world's reserve currency not through natural selection, but through a series of historical arrangements that created lasting asymmetries. From Bretton Woods to Nixon's gold window closure to the petrodollar system—each step embedded American monetary policy deeper into global trade. When the Fed raises rates to cool down Phoenix housing markets, currencies from Istanbul to Jakarta feel the pressure. Reserve currency status is economic empire by design, not accident. The system works, providing liquidity the world needs. But it also means most economies must navigate monetary decisions made for someone else's priorities. short_video.hook: The dollar rules the world, but not by accident
short_video.voiceover: Reserve currency status is empire by other means. The world prices oil in dollars, borrows in dollars, then watches America's central bank make decisions for American workers. This wasn't inevitable. Bretton Woods promised gold backing. Nixon ended that in 1971. What remained was a system where everyone needed dollars but only America could print them. The petrodollar arrangement sealed it permanently. Muslim economies inherit this asymmetry daily, holding their breath when the Fed meets, knowing decisions made for Iowa farmers will ripple through their banking systems.
